description: Average the customer counts over only the support-rep values that actually appear on customer records.

a.request: Counting customers per `SupportRepId` value that appears on customer records (with customers that have no rep forming one group), what is the average number of customers per value? Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 AS cnt FROM Customer GROUP BY SupportRepId)

b.request: Average, across only the distinct SupportRepId values that appear on Customer records (excluding NULL and reps with no customers), of the number of customers per support rep, unrounded.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_customers_per_rep FROM (SELECT SupportRepId, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId) AS t
b.raw: Average, across only the distinct SupportRepId values that appear on Customer records (excluding NULL and reps with no customers), of the number of customers per support rep, unrounded.

d.request: Compute the average, without rounding, of the number of customers per distinct non-null SupportRepId in the Customer table (total customers with a support rep divided by the number of distinct support reps appearing on customer records, excluding employees with no customers).
d.sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT SupportRepId) AS avg_customers_per_rep FROM Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL

c.request: On average, how many customers does each support rep look after? Don't round. Average the customer counts over only the support-rep values that actually appear on customer records.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_customers FROM (SELECT SupportRepId, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId) AS t
